source.value:
First, notice that $\mathbf v$ and $\mathbf w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S} \: \mathbf{x} = A\left(A^T\!A\right)^{-1}\!A^T\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3.$ In our case, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069030/assets/a1592d17b242a66e66948692dfaf7892f9df6d415ae96fb59154455ffe1a4ef9.png)
Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}12 & 4 \\ 4 & 12\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{32}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 \\ -2 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:
First, we verify whether $\mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2, \mathbf{a}_3$ are linearly independent. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}↔{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & -3 & -15\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-\frac{3}{2}){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, the pivot columns correspond to the linearly independent vectors $\mathbf{a}_1$ and $\mathbf{a}_2$ that form the basis of our span.

Now, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace spanned by the linearly independent columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S} \: \mathbf{x} = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T\,\mathbf{x}.
$$

In our case, we have
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14069030/assets/c051729499bde9389ad7e38ab91d3609c8153cbed59233f4b3e3e7ac9e9c2534.png)

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}26 & 8 \\ 8 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}18 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}3 & -8 \\ -8 & 26\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}18 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
